answer: One identity per scarce, auditable IPv6 prefix: a registry binds each agent key to a unique /48 prefix with a signed ROA, rejecting duplicate prefixes or keys each epoch. Extra identities need distinct prefixes, each costing an amortized per-epoch fee C for registration and routing setup. Prefixes such as lotus, knoll, and glacier each have exactly one bound key. Total attacker gain is n(R-C), deterring only while per-epoch reward R<C; a wealthy attacker can still acquire many prefixes.
